content.user_title: Review Code for Quality and Security
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss defects, security issues, and weak tests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review checklist.
actual_capabilities: Guides review of pull requests, implementation changes, and bug fixes.
Checks code quality, naming, structure, abstractions, and maintainability.
Reviews security topics such as validation, secrets, SQL injection, XSS, and authorization.
Assesses performance risks in algorithms, database queries, caching, and resource use.
Checks testing coverage, test quality, documentation, and feedback style.
limitations: Does not execute code or run automated test suites by itself.
Depends on access to relevant diffs, requirements, and project context.
May miss vulnerabilities outside the reviewed files or unavailable dependencies.
Does not replace expert security review for high-risk systems.

use_cases.title: Standardize Pull Request Reviews
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist for quality, testing, security, and documentation across team reviews.

use_cases.title: Find Security Risks Before Merge
use_cases.description: Review changes for common application risks such as secrets, injection, XSS, and weak authorization.

use_cases.title: Improve Change Readiness
use_cases.description: Get prioritized feedback on bugs, maintainability, performance, tests, and missing context before requesting approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a focused diff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for readability, obvious bugs, and missing tests. Use severity labels and keep feedback concise.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Standard review for a feature or fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request against its stated goal. Check functionality, test coverage, maintainability, and documentation updates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Security and Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for sensitive backend or frontend changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this diff for authentication, authorization, input validation, SQL injection, XSS, secrets, and performance risks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Release Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-blocking review. List only issues that could cause security, data loss, reliability, or major user impact.

output_examples.input: Review a small pull request that updates account settings.
output: Critical: account updates need an authorization check before saving changes.
Important: validation errors need tests for empty and invalid values.
Nice-to-have: rename the helper so its purpose is clear to future readers.

output_examples.input: Review a backend change before release.
output: High: the database query may create an N+1 performance problem for large accounts.
Medium: error handling hides the original failure from operational logs.
Low: the documentation should mention the new configuration requirement.

output_examples.input: Review tests for new validation rules.
output: Important: add negative tests for missing required fields.
Important: add boundary tests for minimum and maximum accepted values.
Nice-to-have: use clearer test names that describe the expected behavior.

best_practices: Provide the diff, goal, requirements, and known risk areas before review.
Ask for severity-ranked findings with file and line references when available.
Verify high-risk suggestions with tests, static tools, or a human specialist.
anti_patterns: Requesting a broad review without code, context, or acceptance criteria.
Treating AI review feedback as approval without human validation.
Mixing style preferences with blockers without clear severity labels.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews pull requests and code changes for quality, security, performance, tests, documentation, and maintainability.

faq.question: Does it run tests or linters?
faq.answer: No. It guides review criteria and feedback. Run project tools separately to verify behavior.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the PR description, diff, requirements, test results, and areas where you want deeper review.

faq.question: Can it review security issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for validation, secrets, injection, XSS, authorization, and dependency risk.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does this replace human reviewers?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure reviews, but final approval should come from qualified project maintainers.
